SQLAlchemy 2.0 asyncio "lazy loading" selectinload raiseload AsyncSession docs

Links: [{"title":"The Problem","url":"https://scour.ing/@nmarshall/p/https://dev.to/ayush_kumar_085a0f2c54e3f/fixing-sqlalchemyexcmissinggreenlet-in-fastapi-and-async-sqlalchemy-20-4gha"},{"title":"No project description provided","url":"https://pypi.org/project/async-sqlmodel/0.1.3/"},{"title":"async sqlmodel","url":"https://pypi.org/project/async-sqlmodel"},{"title":"5dMvjNp introducing asynchronous sqlalchemy","url":"https://ep2021.europython.eu/media/conference/slides/5dMvjNp-introducing-asynchronous-sqlalchemy.pdf"},{"title":"async sqlmodel","url":"https://github.com/2jun0/async-sqlmodel"},{"title":"relationship loading techniques in sqlalchemy 4e7d1ff96f75","url":"https://medium.com/@vickypalaniappan12/relationship-loading-techniques-in-sqlalchemy-4e7d1ff96f75"},{"title":"# util/_concurrency_py3k.py","url":"https://sigodd.gouv.bj/mes-ia-odd/micro-service/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py"},{"title":"# util/_concurrency_py3k.py","url":"https://download.hermesedi.duckdns.org/.cache/uv/archive-v0/xvyB33oA02pdPvil/sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py"},{"title":"github.com","url":"https://github.com/fastapi/sqlmodel/issues/74"},{"title":"# util/_concurrency_py3k.py","url":"https://decoder-genetics.wustl.edu/software/conda/lib/python3.1/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py"}]

The error means SQLAlchemy tried to run a database call (a lazy load) from code that isn't running inside its async wrapper. In async sessions, touching an unloaded relationship triggers that failure.

**What causes it**

- Accessing a relationship attribute that wasn't loaded by the original query is the usual trigger. One write-up describes this as the most common pitfall when moving from sync to async SQLAlchemy (the error appears when a relationship such as user.posts was not fetched in the original query).
- In a sync app, SQLAlchemy would quietly run a second query on access. In async code, it can't pause the event loop to do that, so it raises instead (it can't run the query, so it crashes).
- The same thing happens after a commit: expired attributes reload on access, and that reload also raises. One example shows a hero whose fields have expired, so accessing them raises a MissingGreenlet error.

**Fixes**

1. **Eager-load the relationship in the query.** Use `selectinload` or `joinedload` so the related rows arrive with the parent. For example, `select(PirateCrew).options(selectinload(PirateCrew.members))` runs a second query up front instead of on access. selectinload performs a second SQL query immediately after the first, to load the related objects.
2. **Await the attribute explicitly.** Libraries like async-sqlmodel offer awaitable accessors, so you write `team = await hero.awt_team` rather than `hero.team`. Async-SQLModel is an extension module of SQLModel, making it compatible with asynchronous programming, especially useful when lazy-loading relational fields asynchronously.
3. **Avoid implicit loads after commit.** Setting `expire_on_commit=False` on the session, or reloading the object, keeps attributes from expiring. This is standard SQLAlchemy practice, and I didn't verify it in these results.

**Where the message comes from**

SQLAlchemy raises this from its concurrency helper when a sync-style call runs outside the greenlet context. The source says the helper checks for a greenlet provider and raises MissingGreenlet with the "Was IO attempted in an unexpected place?" message if none is found. This confirms the cause: I/O happened somewhere it shouldn't.

The search turned up mostly official SQLAlchemy docs and third-party write-ups. Lazy loading doesn't work under asyncio, so the usual fix is to choose an eager or explicit loader for each relationship.

**Lazy loading is off the table with asyncio.** The 2.0 docs say so directly in the column loading section, noting that lazy loading is not available when using Asynchronous I/O (asyncio). The 1.4 asyncio docs add that special care must be taken to avoid lazy loading or other expired-attribute access involving ORM relationships and column attributes when using the default `AsyncSession` mode.

**selectinload is the usual eager loader.** The 1.4 asyncio docs show `select(A).options(selectinload(A.bs))` and note that without it, accessing `A.bs` would raise an asyncio exception. selectinload performs a second SQL query immediately after the first, to load the related objects. That is a third-party article, not the official docs.

**raiseload turns accidental lazy loads into errors.** A blog by Miguel Grinberg suggests that a safe choice is to change all the lazy loading relationships to lazy='raise', so that they raise an error if SQLAlchemy would need to lazy load them. You can then pass an eager loader in `options()` where you need the data. For deferred columns, the official docs describe using `raiseload` with `load_only()` or `defer()` so that an exception is raised when the attribute is accessed, indicating that the need to query the database for this column was not expected.

**Related option.** One third-party guide uses `lazy="raise_on_sql"` instead, which only raises when SQL would actually be emitted. Raise an error if you forget to load data is the stated purpose. I couldn't confirm this against the official docs, so check it there before relying on it.

**Where to read more.** The official "Relationship Loading Techniques" page in the 2.0 docs covers the loader strategies, and the Asynchronous I/O extension page covers `AsyncSession` specifics. The search didn't return the 2.0 asyncio page itself, only a 1.4 mirror, so verify version-specific details against docs.sqlalchemy.org.

**MissingGreenlet** (SQLAlchemy 2.0.54, the version shown on the page)

**Description:** The page says, "A call to the async DBAPI was initiated outside the greenlet spawn context" that SQLAlchemy's AsyncIO proxy classes normally set up. In other words, database I/O ran in a place where it couldn't be awaited.

**Typical causes:**
- I/O happened in an unexpected place, using a calling pattern that doesn't use `await`.
- With the ORM, this is almost always lazy loading. The page notes that lazy loading "is not directly supported under asyncio without additional steps and/or alternate loader patterns."

**Suggested fixes:** The section doesn't spell out specific fixes. resulting_evidence:
## Findings: SQLAlchemy `MissingGreenlet` with SQLAlchemy 2.x

**Bottom line:** The official SQLAlchemy 2.0 docs say that with the ORM, this error is almost always implicit lazy loading inside an async session. That matches your `project.md` observation. The fix is to load the relationship explicitly before access, or to make the access awaitable. Your root cause is still unreproduced, so these are documented patterns, not a confirmed diagnosis.

### What the official docs establish

- **Error meaning:** SQLAlchemy's [error xd2s](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/errors.html#error-xd2s) says "A call to the async DBAPI was initiated outside the greenlet spawn context." For the ORM, it says the cause is "almost always lazy loading," which "is not directly supported under asyncio without additional steps and/or alternate loader patterns." The page points to the "Preventing Implicit IO when Using AsyncSession" section for mitigation. It does not list specific fixes itself.
- **Avoid implicit IO:** The [asyncio extension docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html) say "Using traditional asyncio, the application needs to avoid any points at which IO-on-attribute access may occur." They suggest the `AsyncAttrs` mixin, which exposes attributes as awaitables.
- **Eager loading:** The same page calls `selectinload()` "the most useful eager loading strategy" and says relationships can be declared with `lazy="raise"` so they "will not attempt to emit SQL." The `raiseload()` option is not named there.
- **Expiry after commit:** The page says `expire_on_commit` "should normally be set to False when using asyncio." After a commit, expired attributes reload on access, and that reload is implicit IO.

### Applicability to this project

- `requirements.txt` pins `SQLAlchemy==2.0.43` and `asyncpg==0.30.0`. The docs I read are for 2.0.54, the version shown on the pages. The 2.0.43 behavior described above is documented but not version-verified. asyncpg is the driver underneath, but the error comes from SQLAlchemy's greenlet bridge, so the driver version is unlikely to be the cause. I did not check this directly.
- The fixture has no application code, so I could not check the session configuration, the query shapes, or where the relationship is read.
- Your observation (reading an unloaded relationship outside the awaited query) is consistent with the documented cause. Two other documented triggers to rule out are access after `commit()` on an expired object, and `expire_on_commit` left at its default `True`.

### Recommended next steps (not yet verified here)

1. **Find the access site.** Read the full traceback and identify the line that touches the relationship. This is the discriminating check; the traceback should show whether it's a lazy load or an expired-attribute reload.
2. **Eager-load at the query.** Add `selectinload(Model.relationship)` to the `select()` that produced the object. This is the documented default.
3. **Make the access explicit.** If the access is in code you can't restructure, use `AsyncAttrs` and await the attribute. Verify the exact accessor name in the docs before using it.
4. **Set `expire_on_commit=False`** on the async session if it is currently `True`, after confirming the rest of the app doesn't rely on refreshed values after commit.
5. **Guard against regressions.** Use `lazy="raise"` on relationships so accidental lazy loads fail loudly in tests. A third-party source mentions `lazy="raise_on_sql"`, but I did not confirm that in the official docs.
6. **Verify locally.** Reproduce with a minimal async test against 2.0.43 that reads the unloaded relationship. Then confirm the fix makes that test pass. Documented support alone does not prove the fix works in your app.

### Sources

- [SQLAlchemy error xd2s (MissingGreenlet), 2.0.54 docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/errors.html#error-xd2s)
- [SQLAlchemy asyncio extension, 2.0.54 docs](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html)
- Search leads, not verified against the sources: [dev.to write-up on fixing MissingGreenlet](https://scour.ing/@nmarshall/p/https://dev.to/ayush_kumar_085a0f2c54e3f/fixing-sqlalchemyexcmissinggreenlet-in-fastapi-and-async-sqlalchemy-20-4gha), [Miguel Grinberg, SQLAlchemy 2 in Practice ch. 7](https://blog.miguelgrinberg.com/post/sqlalchemy-2-in-practice---chapter-7-asynchronous-sqlalchemy)
